items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, creamery 1891, Gideon Vose first president to 1911.

Story 1 gives Article VII's core rule (pay by pounds of butterfat found by test, not by weight). The 'test of the station where he delivers governs' clause appears only in Section B, but no REQUIRED line bundles this item, so the core fact carries it.
Quotes Falke: 'Under payment by weight nothing that follows would have cost any man a dollar'; calls Article VII the hinge.

Partial roster: Teague named as bookkeeper (Story 3), Sill as buttermaker at Larrow Green (Story 2). Effie Loomis and the 1901/1905 dates are absent from the whole sheet; credited on the list-item core-fact rule.
Section A calls Selby Vose 'manager' but never states he was Gideon's son or that he took the post in 1913. Both appear only in Sections B/E, and credit cannot travel into A.
The 'station gain' ledger line is nowhere in Section A. It appears only in B3, D2, C3 and F.
Story 2: seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.

Section A never describes the working system: no weighing at the intake, no composite sample per patron, no percent read off the graduated neck, no cream shipped / skim returned. Only 'a reading is taken off the pipette's own charge.'
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice line-by-line with 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c. and the correct $77.93 total.
Story 3: 'a steady 0.19 points, present in every month of the year alike, winter and flush season both... flat as a floor.'

Story 2 states the reading rests wholly on the pipette's own charge with 'no independent standard to compare against inside the plant', so the defect was invisible from the first day. The burette / none-in-the-county detail is missing but the proposition is stated.
Keddie hired from the 1896 opening day, tester twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
No description anywhere in Section A of the test book's columns, the one-hand keeping, or corrections crossed and initialed.

Credited under the key's own clause ('a solver that gives the two figures anywhere in Section A has earned it'): Story 3 carries 3.61 recorded and ~3.80 true. The summary leaf itself, the 1896 season and the 1898 step are never mentioned - a lenient award.
Section A mentions only 'a question mark in his book after the unexplained 1911 anomaly'. The 8 May / 10 July dates, the nine weeks and the 3.80-to-3.61 return are given only in D1.
Story 4: Orra is Ansel's wife; 'Emmet Brant - Orra's own brother, the largest patron on the Bottom'.

1919 circular over the manager's signature accusing the patrons of watering is fully told (Story 4). Keddie's own 17 March 1925 statement is absent; item is not bundled by a REQUIRED line, so the lead fact carries it.
'dying in 1934 still under the valley's unspoken suspicion' - 1934 is the only bolded element.
Hessel Bottom's six farms (Story 2/5); Emmet Brant the largest patron (Story 4).
Brant's weigh book appears in Section A only as an item on the 1925 exhibit list. Neither the 1 January 1897 start nor the fact that the two scales agreed is stated in Section A.

'From 1902, Ostrey Hollow's patrons began complaining publicly that their milk tested lower...'. The run never states the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19 nor derives a Larrow Green average from 0.19, so the conflation gate does not fire (it does loosely give Larrow Green as '~3.78-3.80').
Grigg's 1908 committee and the wet-pasture finding are given as a theory advanced, never as fact. The Jan-Feb-Mar sampling appears only in E and F.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional-loss point appear only in Section C2 - not in Section A.
Story 8: 'She also borrowed Roy Brant's family ledger (returned the same year)' in 1958.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, across Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd. Gives both 1913 and 1914 and declares them unreconcilable - which the key expressly allows; no deduction.
From 1915, four of the six Hessel Bottom farms hauled over in the summer flush and back to Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year.
REQUIRED met: another county, their own glassware, and a book never compared with Ostrey Hollow's ('it never entered his head') - three of the four elements.
Sixteen seasons 1915-1930, the same four men, averaging ~3.80 against the station's 3.61 - the 0.19 difference stated as levels rather than as a difference.
'the single clearest piece of evidence... that the milk itself was never at fault, since the same cows produced normal test results the moment they were measured on different glass.'
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, ran it after his death in 1941 and supplied the full sixteen-season table to Ivy Keddie in 1958.
'Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector for the Ordell circuit since 1907' - the contested start year taken correctly. The 1936 end is not given in Section A.
The lactometer runs and the never-once-found-water finding appear only in F2 (and there dated 'from 1908'). Nothing in Section A.
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned - correctly preferred over the planted 12 July.
The run says nobody drew a connection, but never states that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation - the bolded content of the item.

No 28 June order / 2 July acknowledgment dates ('ordered and in use within the month'), and the post-condemnation average is given as 'roughly 3.80-3.85', absorbing the planted 3.85. Item lost; see deductions.
'the condemned crate was simply carried up to the loft over the intake room and left there' - this item's own aspect (where it went in 1923).
'The Hessel Bottom patrons petitioned the Association in January 1925.'
Board under Alonzo Frick, three sessions, 17 March 1925 at Ashlin and twice at the station's own weigh room; award 4 May 1925.
All three explanations argued (water by Vose, theft obliquely by Teague, wet hay via the 1908 report) and no formal finding of cause.
The four-book exhibit list named exactly, including Strawn's 1923 notebook, with the crate sitting unmentioned in the loft above.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding; award 4 May 1925 of $3,800 'without admission'. Missing only 'charged to the station account'.

Section A never says the award was one fifth of the $19,000 lost, nor that it was charged to the account the loss had been accruing into as 'gain' since 1898. Instead it asserts the claim as '$19,600 or 67,000 lb' - two planted errors (see deductions).
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, Bulletin co-written with Professor Leland Vaught.

Shows the assembly - the crate, Brant's ledger, Cudd's independent Alder Corners figures 'as corroboration' - though it never states the never-in-the-same-room point and omits the test book, Strawn's notebooks and the ledgers from that list.
February 1958, the loft over the old intake room, the 1923 crate, nine surviving pipettes.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, 16.72 c.c. against a 17.6 mark, a consistent 5% ('one part in twenty'). The explicit 0.88 c.c. is given only in C4(b) but 5% is 0.95 of the mark.
Section A carries 1 May 1897 (Story 2), 12 June 1923 (Story 6), 3.61/3.80/0.19 (Story 3) and the 5% shortfall 'exactly matching the historical test gap' (Story 8).

REQUIRED all four inside Section A. Story 8 gives only '76,000 lb / $19,000 ... over 25 affected delivery years (worked in Section C)' - no 40,000,000 lb or 1,600,000/yr in Section A, and no ledger identity anywhere in Section A.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clearing him, 'twenty-four years after his death'. The 35- and 33-year intervals are not given.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter, Duncan is Ansel's son; resolves 'great-niece' via Duncan's family notes and Falke's own printed self-correction.
Second cousins, with the full derivation through Orra/Emmet and Duncan/Roy; Oram's 'first cousin once removed' rejected.

ABSTENTION ITEM ASSERTED: 'I resolve this in favor of full siblings, since it is Emmet's own son's first-hand, deliberate claim' - a headline verdict, repeated in E item 3. It does correctly note the answer does not change either way, but the key requires a declared inability to settle. See deductions.
Gideon Vose, his father; 'nephew' rejected with two first-person rebuttals.
The man who accused the patrons was enforcing his own father's Article VII, which made the station's test decide every patron's pay.
ABSTENTION ITEM ASSERTED: 'None, on the best evidence available... I conclude the families were not related, and the belief that they were is valley gossip.' See deductions.

Lays out the record accurately: Duncan's flat first-person denial against Oram's self-admitted hedge with no names, generation or mechanism. It does not observe that no document names or denies a link, nor that a family denial is not a record.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95% of the mark, 5% short, 'one part in twenty'. Explicitly rejects the planted 16.27 cascade.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19, with the reciprocal check.
40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb; explicitly prefers 40 M over the planted 44 M.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; $3,800 received = one fifth / 20%. Both money and fraction given. Rejects the planted 27 cents.
3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60; 7,200 lb true; 360 lb owed. Correctly argues the correction is proportional, not additive.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40 - the key's exact answer, using the 1910 price.
76,000; names both denominators explicitly - 5.00% of the delivered total, 5.26% of the credited total. Correctly avoids the '5.26% of the true fat' trap.
$77.93, primary invoice preferred over the planted $77.39.
72 pipettes (six dozen), each short 0.88 c.c.; breaks the 'five dozen' error with the 72 x $0.35 = $25.20 line check.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, '26 years and about six weeks'; money runs over 25 full delivery years because the part years at each end are excluded.
CORRECT ABSTENTION: 'This cannot be settled precisely... I report both rather than pick one', with both poles and why they cannot be reconciled.
'The variable was the measuring instrument alone' - the station's own measure broken, a borrowed one substituted.
Four constants named: same tester, same herds, same pasture, essentially the same season.

8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, defended against the planted 'six weeks' by showing the two carriers are probably one source. Result given as 'rose to about the true level... fell back the instant the station's own glass resumed' rather than the numerals 3.80/3.61.

Both halves present: rules out theft and feed/pasture in one stroke because the deficiency travelled with the instrument; and states limits (not the size or mechanism, not specifically the pipettes, not constancy over 26 years).
Four reasons from different sources; three are on the key's list - the 1911 interval (Keddie's log), the station-gain surplus (the Association's own books), the Alder Corners records (Rosalie Cudd).
Independence argued on different methods, custodians and eras; explicitly states all four would still hold had the 1958 measurement never happened.

ABSTENTION ITEM ASSERTED: 'Partially. He is on record as having raised the station-gain discrepancy directly with manager Selby Vose once, in 1916, and was told to let it alone' - treats one narrator's uncorroborated claim as 'one documented exception'. See deductions.
Answers the literal question yes: 'manager Selby Vose knew the tests ran low well before the 1923 condemnation.'

REQUIRED three of five, credited anywhere in B-G: manager from 1913 (E item 11), the annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line under his signature (D3, B3), the 1919 water circular (B3, F2).

ABSTENTION ITEM ASSERTED: goes past the literal question to 'he knew, at the latest from 1916, because he was told to his face and chose institutional silence over investigation' - the station-gain-line-told-him route the key names explicitly as an A03 assertion. See deductions.

Cap reached. Rows resolved with a stated method: Keddie's start 1895 vs 4 May 1896 (documentary date over third-generation lore); Brant's weigh book to 1 Jan 1897 over 1898/1900 (two independent sources, generational date-creep); Orra's birth 1866 over 1868 (age-at-death arithmetic); Grigg's 1908 sampling (report against its own covering letter); the cheese factory declared unreconcilable with the method stated. Row 15 (Vose manager 1913) was flagged unresolved rather than resolved.

Cap reached, with a dedicated 'two narrators carry the same wrong value' subsection: 12 July 1923 (Vose's address + Rundle, broken by the circuit book and its photostat); 'nephew' (Toland r01 + Rundle r12); Bulletin 214's '0.20' (Grigg + Kepp, broken by the verbatim 0.05); 27 cents (Sill + Kepp, broken by ledger arithmetic); plus eleven survivors (Rundle + Chronicle) and five dozen pipettes.

A10 earned: Article VII's year declared 'genuinely undetermined' with the three poles and the absence of any contemporaneous document. A04 lost - the short lot is asserted as 'almost certainly' a regrooved-mold accident. A06 (whose measure was borrowed in 1911) never raised at all.
A dedicated self-contradiction subsection: Grigg's letter vs its own report, Bulletin 471 against itself, Rundle's in-press retraction, Duncan's 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'.
Names the 1897 pipette lot, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95% of truth; derives 0.19 as 5% of a ~3.80 milk; explains onset (1 May 1897), cessation (12 June 1923) and why nothing on the farms had to change.
Watering named (Vose's 1919 circular) and defeated with Strawn's lactometer runs and the Alder Corners records for the same four men. (The lactometer years are misdated 'from 1908' - see deductions.)
Theft named (Teague) and defeated with the station-gain surplus - cream arriving heavy, not light, in the accuser's own books - plus the 1911 interval.
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated with Bulletin 214's actual 0.05-in-winter/nothing-in-summer against a flat 0.19, plus the 1911 interval.
ABSTENTION ITEM ASSERTED: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.' A flat verdict sentence. The supporting observations are right but the key requires declining. See deductions.

CORRECT ABSTENTION: 'one of the record's real, unresolved contradictions... I do not think the sources let us choose between them', with both poles (Frick vs Duncan) and their uncorroborated character.
153 words against a hard cap of 150.

Five series reachable: the Association's ledgers, the inspector's notebook, the invoice, the 1958 burette measurement, and the hearing chairman's memoir standing for the arbitration record. 'Letters', 'a diary' and 'a bulletin' are not among the nine; the station test book, Brant's weigh book and the Alder Corners book are absent.
Clean: watering/theft/pasture attributed to 'contemporaries blamed', and every headline number correct (16.72, 17.6, 5%, 76,000 lb, 1897, 1923, 1925, 1958).
Four of six, covering both ends: 5% shortfall, from 1897, 76,000 lb, explained in 1958. Ansel Keddie named; Ivy is only 'his granddaughter'.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Story 7 asserts the patrons' claim as '$19,600' (planted error F081 / X41; canon $19,000), unflagged and unreconciled with its own C1 answer of $19,000
Corruption: Story 7 asserts '67,000 lb of butterfat' (planted error F080 / X48; canon 76,000 lb), unflagged and unreconciled with its own C1/C3 answer of 76,000 lb
Corruption: Story 6 gives the post-condemnation station average as 'roughly 3.80-3.85', absorbing the planted 3.85 (X51/X90, NT-3) into its own claim
Corruption: F2 dates Strawn's lactometer visits 'from 1908 onward', absorbing the planted 1908 circuit start (X102, NT-23) and contradicting its own correct 1907 in Story 6
Gullibility (A01): B4 asserts 'None, on the best evidence available... I conclude the families were not related'
Gullibility (A03): D3 asserts Vose knew the tests were wrong - 'he knew, at the latest from 1916, because he was told to his face and chose institutional silence over investigation'
Gullibility (A04): Story 2 and F1 assert the short lot was 'almost certainly' a regrooved-mold accident, in the sheet's own voice with no declining qualifier
Gullibility (A07): F5 answers 'No' on whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware
Gullibility (A08): B2 asserts 'I resolve this in favor of full siblings' (repeated at E item 3)
Gullibility (A09): D2 asserts the bookkeeper did question the entries - 'Partially. He is on record as having raised the station-gain discrepancy... in 1916'
